concerns.text: Task T002 pins package versions with '[UNRESOLVED-CLAIM]' markers (e.g., 'torch==2.1.0+cpu [UNRESOLVED-CLAIM: c_0f4f203b — status=not_enough_info]'). This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and FR-030, which mandate that dependencies be pinned in a runnable state before execution. A task delivering a requirements file with unresolved claims fails to satisfy the constraint of a reproducible environment.

Task T012 includes a citation '2011.02803, https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02803' embedded directly in the task description text rather than as a verified reference. While the URL is valid, the task description format mixes implementation logic with unverified citation claims, risking 'Verified Accuracy' (Constitution Principle II) violations if the citation is not formally resolved in the research layer before code generation.

Task T021 explicitly states it is 'deviating from Spec FR-004' by using native ground truth instead of upsampled ground truth. While the Plan.md authorizes this deviation, the task itself does not include a deliverable to formally update the spec (that is deferred to T036). This creates a state where the implementation task violates the current spec's FR-004 without an immediate, atomic correction mechanism in the task flow, risking a temporary 'Single Source of Truth' (Constitution Principle IV) breach.

Task T022 explicitly states it is 'deviating from Spec SC-005' by using paired t-test/Wilcoxon instead of one-sample t-test. Similar to T021, this task implements a constraint violation of the current spec (SC-005) without an immediate atomic update to the spec document, relying on a future task (T036) to resolve the contradiction. This is a semantic weakening of the current spec's acceptance criteria.

Task T036 is a documentation task ('Update spec.md') rather than an implementation task. The spec amendments (FR-004, SC-005) are critical constraints that must be satisfied *before* the implementation tasks (T021, T022) that violate them are executed. Placing the spec update as a 'Polish' phase task (Phase 6) allows the implementation to proceed against a contradictory spec, violating the 'Single Source of Truth' principle during the execution of T021 and T022.
